newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called up on Tuesday expiry, IPE gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called up on Tuesday expiry, IPE gains.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called higher Monday on expected short covering related to the Tuesday expiry in the May contract and gains by Brent futures on London's IPE.
"The May/June (crude) spread is going to blow out a bit more, but the move is artificial because it's only on expiry," said a New York crude trader.
Crude was called 20 to 25 cents higher a barrel. Heating oil and gasoline were called 0.25 to 0.50 cent a gallon higher. May Brent was 35 cents a barrel higher at $18.27 on the IPE.

Prices were also seen supported on concerns that Iraq was sending helicopters on Monday to pick up returning Moslem pilgrims from the Saudi border despite a ban by the United States and other Western powers on Iraqi flights in the area.
But, when Iraq flew the pilgrims on April 9 to Mecca for the haj pilgrimage, the U.N. Security Council issued only a statement calling on Iraq not to fly more planes without its consent.

Still, dealers said the breach of the "no-fly zone" has prompted concern that it could hurt the U.N.-Iraq oil-for-food accord whereby the U.N. allowed Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil every six months, on a renewable basis, in exchange for food and other humanitarian aid.

Also supporting prices was news OPEC's president Libyan Oil Minister Abdalla el-Badri called for OPEC members to restrain oil output to help support crude prices. But, OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman said it was not yet claar whether there has been any response to the request.
On Friday, May crude ended 49 cents higher at $19.91 a barrel. May heating oil ended 0.68 cent higher at 54.68 cents a gallon while May gasoline ended up 0.79 cent at 61.49 cents a gallon.
